messages.author: 77163672d51fa17c
messages.subject: stan model in batch job
parts:
In a simulation study, I would like run the same stan models on different data sets at the same time. I am the rstan interface, and SLURM (Linux) to generate the batch job. Unfortunately, this results in the following errors:

checkForRemoteErrors(val): 7 nodes produced errors; first error: unable to load shared object '/tmp/RtmpisFRKa/file3966e77c594.so':
/tmp/RtmpisFRKa/file3966e77c594.so: file too short

and

In writeBin(dso@.CXXDSOMISC$dso_bin, libLFile) :
problem writing to connection

Is there an elegant way to prevent this issue? I see two possible workarounds, but I hope there is a better way: (a) copy my original .stan script to a task-specific script, so each task effectively has its own stan script and it's own .so, hopefully circumventing clashes OR (b) load the model using auto_write=FALSE. Downside is that I have wait for the compilation to occur every time I run my script. Both are rather ugly.

It is probably difficult for you to replicate this issue, because it requires to have the same environment. Still, I hope that your deeper understanding of the inner works can lead to a suggestion. What is suspect is happening, is that the simultaneous tasks try to write to the same .so file, while another one is trying to use it at the same time.

Thanks in advance,
Stijn.

In a simulation study, I would like run the same stan models on different data sets at the same time. I am the rstan interface, and SLURM (Linux) to generate the batch job. Unfortunately, this results in the following errors:

In the next version of rstan on Linux, it will use parallel::mclapply() rather than parallel::makePSOCKCluster(), so hopefully this will not occur anymore. There is a branch on GitHub, but it pretty much does what is suggested in the example for sflist2stanfit.

Ben
